purpose: Methamphetamine is an FDA-approved prescription medication used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and, in some cases, short-term obesity management when other treatments have not worked. It helps improve focus and attention in people with ADHD. It is only used medically in very specific situations under close doctor supervision.
how_it_works: This medication works by increasing the levels of certain natural chemicals in your brain, like dopamine and norepinephrine, that help with focus and impulse control. Think of it as helping your brain's communication system work more efficiently. This boost in brain chemicals helps calm the restlessness and improve concentration in people with ADHD.
common_side_effects: Decreased appetite and weight loss, trouble sleeping or insomnia, faster heart rate, dry mouth, headache, increased blood pressure, feeling restless or nervous, stomach upset or nausea, and mood changes.
warnings: This medication has a very HIGH potential for abuse, dependence, and addiction — it is a Schedule II controlled substance. Do not take more than prescribed. It can cause serious heart problems including heart attack or stroke, especially in people with existing heart conditions. It may cause or worsen mental health issues such as anxiety, psychosis, or aggression. Do not use if you have a history of drug abuse. It is not safe during pregnancy. Never share this medication with anyone else.
typical_dosing: For ADHD in adults and children 6 years and older, the typical starting dose is 5 mg once or twice daily, and the doctor may slowly adjust it based on how you respond. It is usually taken in the morning to avoid sleep problems. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
